tavily.text:
The sources do not provide direct instructions for setting up and installing the boltons Python package. However, they do mention how to run tests using `pytest`, including running all tests with `pytest` or `python -m pytest`, specific test files with `pytest tests/test_cacheutils.py`, and specific test functions with `pytest tests/test_cacheutils.py::test_lru_add`. The sources also list various test files and their contents but do not specify installation steps for the boltons package.
To install the boltons Python library from the GitHub repository, use the command `pip install boltons`. The repository specifies that it is built with Python 3.10 on Ubuntu 22.04 and documentation is built with Sphinx. The library includes various utilities such as file saving, ordered dictionaries, priority queues, and more. The sources do not provide a definitive answer to the current date or version count.
To install the "boltons" package, you can use pip, the Python package installer. The PyPI page for "boltons" indicates that it is a set of over 230 BSD-licensed, pure-Python utilities. To install it, you can use the command `pip install boltons`. Additionally, there is a typing stub package available for "boltons" named "types-boltons" which can be installed with `pip install types-boltons`. This typing stub package aims to provide accurate annotations for "boltons" version 26.1.* and is part of the typeshed project.
Mar 1, 2013 · Boltons boltons should be builtins. Boltons is a set of over 230 BSD-licensed, pure-Python utilities in the same spirit as — and yet conspicuously missing from — the standard library, including: Atomic file saving, bolted on with fileutils A highly-optimized OrderedMultiDict, in dictutils Two types of PriorityQueue, in queueutils
Sep 6, 2026 · Typing stubs for boltons This is a type stub package for the boltons package. It can be used by type checkers to check code that uses boltons. This version of types-boltons aims to provide accurate annotations for boltons==26.1.*. This package is part of the typeshed project. All fixes for types and metadata should be contributed there.
